decisions.rationale: 'Myotonia levior' names one specific disease (a milder dominant myotonia) that can be linked to a single definition, so it is annotated as a Specific Disease.
'chloride channel disorder' refers to a family of diseases caused by chloride channel dysfunction (e.g., myotonia congenita and other chloride channelopathies), not one specific disease.
decisions.guideline_section: What to Annotate §1 (Disease Class); Examples 10-11 (grey-area family terms)

decisions.rationale: 'dominant non-dystrophic myotonias' is explicitly described as a group of disorders, a family of multiple specific diseases.
'disorders' is a very general term referring to the group without naming a disease, similar to excluded general terms such as 'disease' or 'syndrome'.
'myogenic muscle stiffness' describes a clinical symptom/phenotype characteristic of the myotonias rather than a disease name, so it is not a disease mention.
decisions.guideline_section: What to Annotate §1 (disease mention criterion); What NOT to Annotate §4

decisions.rationale: 'Dominant myotonia congenita' is a named specific disease (the dominant form, Thomsen's disease); the full phrase is the minimum necessary span for the most specific form.
decisions.guideline_section: What to Annotate §1 (Specific Disease); §5 (minimum necessary span)

decisions.rationale: 'Thomsens disease' is a named specific disease with a single definition (myotonia congenita dominant form).
'dominant myotonias sensitive to potassium' refers to a group of related diseases caused by SCN4A point mutations, a family of multiple specific diseases.
'myotonia levior' is a specific disease named in the text, distinct from Thomsen's disease, and is annotated as a Specific Disease.
'myotonia' used generically in 'later onset of myotonia' refers to the family of myotonic disorders rather than one specific disease, so it is treated as a Disease Class.
decisions.guideline_section: What to Annotate §1 (Disease Class); Examples 10-11 (grey-area family terms)

decisions.rationale: 'Thomsens disease' is a named specific disease used as the comparison disease in the text.
decisions.guideline_section: What to Annotate §1 (Specific Disease); §4 duplicate mentions

decisions.rationale: 'myotonia levior' is repeated as a specific disease mention in the sentence about the family diagnosis; duplicate mentions are annotated.
'disorder' is a general anaphoric term referring back to myotonia levior without naming a disease, and general terms like 'disorder' are excluded.
'Thomsens disease' is a named specific disease mentioned as the disease to which myotonia levior is compared.
'Thomsen' is a disease name used as a modifier of the noun 'pedigree' (a typical Thomsen pedigree), so it is annotated as a Modifier.
'Thomsens disease' is a named specific disease for the family previously diagnosed with it.
'recessive myotonia' refers to a specific recessive form of myotonia (Becker-type) linked to a known CLCN1 deletion, which can be defined as one specific disease.
decisions.guideline_section: What to Annotate §1 (Specific Disease); §5 (minimum necessary span)
